prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Document: Management by Trajectory (MBT) Concept of Operations (ConOps), far-term ATM vision for the National Airspace System (NAS); interprets Trajectory Based Operations (TBO), consistent with ICAO TBO Concept. Far-term: NAS and most aircraft support Aeronautical Telecommunications Network-Baseline 2 (ATN-B2). Near-term constrained by NAS Enterprise Architecture (EA)/NextGen. Current NAS: automation predicts trajectories from flight plans; controllers issue open tactical clearances; Time Based Flow Management (TBFM). MBT: FAA and airspace users negotiate closed four-dimensional trajectories (4DTs) for all IFR aircraft; aircraft shall follow assigned 4DTs. NAS Constraint Service publishes constraints; traffic management automation translates TMIs into flight-specific constraints; aircraft send 4DT intent; conflicts resolved by modifying constraints. Data comm delivers 4DTs to Flight Management System (FMS); electronic flight bag (EFB). Negotiating controller coordinates with traffic management coordinators (TMCs). Near-term: controllers retain separation; one FMS Required Time of Arrival (RTA); CPDLC; SWIM; mixed equipage. Far-term: digital trajectories; voice for immediate action; TCAS/ACAS evolves from UAS detect-and-avoid, converging with Advanced Interval Management (A-IM, self-separation for merging to runways/constrained resources without repeated time-constraint updates); aircraft send planned avoidance maneuvers to ground automation. TBFM extends into en route; miles-in-trail (MIT) and minute-in-trail (MINIT) reduced near-term, eliminated far-term. Required Time Performance (RTP) complements Required Navigation Performance (RNP) for time-of-arrival control (TOAC); RTP-Y = 95% crossing-time error interval (s). All aircraft shall be certified to some RTP level. Users: flight operations centers, private service providers, UAS, space launch, airships, rotorcraft, on-demand. Scope: airborne only; surface interface exchanges takeoff/landing predictions, runway assignments, pushback planning. Traffic Flow Management (TFM) separate: selects TMIs; MBT assigns TMI-compliant trajectories. GDPs/AFPs near-term unchanged; operator chooses takeoff time to meet Controlled Time of Arrival (CTA). Flights kept on closed, de-conflicted trajectories ≥30 min ahead, possibly increasing sector capacity. Research needed: uncertainty-vs-flexibility tradeoff; conservative TFM delay release causes repeated trajectory

U0112: Definitions This chapter presents definitions and discussions of key terminology and concepts. 2.1 Trajectory In the context of MBT, a three-dimensional trajectory (3DT) is a description of an aircraft’s path in space.
U0113: A 3DT is often visualized as a string or tube through space, and described by two dimensions in a horizontal plane (e.g., longitude and latitude) and one vertical dimension (the aircraft’s altitude).
